headline: Draft tree ordinance discussed, with fee, penalty, and enforcement changes planned before council introduction.
summary: A revised draft of the tree ordinance would require a permit to remove five or more established trees. Fees, penalties, and enforcement drew the most comments, and several members said the $700 per tree replacement cost is too high. The chair plans to bring the draft to the City Council on Monday, with more changes to come.
discussion: Replacement tree fee: Members said the estimated $700 per tree replacement cost is too high. Ideas included a lower fee, a waiver for the first few trees, and a fee cut for applicants who plant replacement trees.
Penalties: Members asked whether fines could be higher, such as $300 per tree per day. The attorney said state law caps fines at $300 per offense, so a per-day fine would be hard to set up.
Enforcement of replacement trees: Members discussed whether the Forestry Division or the Commission should check that replacement trees are planted. The Forestry Division has a staff of two.
Effective date and look-back period: The start date was shortened from 180 days to 60 days. Members discussed a look-back period to limit clear-cutting before the law takes effect.
